stimulus.text: Photograph of the American delegates leaving D.A.R. Hall in Washington during the Washington Naval Conference, 1921. Men in overcoats and hats walk down the stone steps of the hall. The photograph's own caption names Elihu Root and Secretary of State Charles Evans Hughes in front, with Senator Henry Cabot Lodge and Senator Oscar Underwood behind.
stimulus.source_note: American delegates leaving D.A.R. Hall, Washington, D.C., during the World Disarmament Conference, 1921. Library of Congress, LCCN2002697195; public domain. The catalog gives the date as September 11, 1921, while the caption printed on the negative reads 11/9/21; the day is not stated in the questions.

source: original; stimulus photograph, American delegates leaving D.A.R. Hall, 1921, Library of Congress, public domain
stem: The photograph shows American delegates at the Washington Naval Conference of 1921-1922. The conference is best known for which of the following?

options.text: Admitting the United States into the League of Nations
options.misconception: The Senate never approved joining the League, and the Washington Conference did not change that.

options.text: Limiting the size of the great powers' battleship fleets
Ending American military occupations in Latin America
options.misconception: The occupations in Latin America ended later, in the 1930s, under the Good Neighbor Policy.

options.text: Placing an embargo on arms sales to warring nations
options.misconception: The arms embargo came with the Neutrality Acts of the 1930s, not with the 1921 conference.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the Senate refused to join the League, and the Washington Conference said nothing about membership.
rationales.B: The conference set limits on battleship tonnage, with a ten-year halt on building new battleships.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Marines stayed in Nicaragua and Haiti into the 1930s, and their withdrawal came under the Good Neighbor Policy.
rationales.D: Background from the books: banning arms sales to belligerents was the Neutrality Act of 1935, fourteen years later.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows the American delegates at the 1921-1922 Washington Naval Conference.
2. Secretary of State Charles Evans Hughes opened the conference by proposing that the great powers scrap battleships already being built.
3. The Five-Power Treaty that followed set battleship tonnage ratios and a ten-year halt on new battleship construction.
4. The aim was to stop a costly naval arms race, not to join the League or police Latin America.
Remember: when a 1920s conference is about ships, look for disarmament, not new commitments.
